inputsClass.description:
Announce the message when it CHANGES while this banner is already on screen — a session countdown, a connection banner that updates, a persistent status bar flipping to degraded.

Off by default, because a banner already present at page load would interrupt the screen reader mid-read, and an assertive one would cut off whatever was being announced.

This will NOT announce a banner that appears. A live region must be in the accessibility tree before its content changes, so mounting an already-populated live banner is not a content change and announces nothing. If you need an ARRIVING message announced, keep your own live region in the layout from first render and write into it, and leave this off.

Compact pill for filter selection or token display.

  • type="filter" (default): a toggle button — click flips selected (aria-pressed exposed). Mono-exclusivity across a group is consumer-owned via selectedChange.

components.description:
Single-file row inside mud-file-input, or standalone in any file list (consumer-driven upload progress, read-only summaries).

Example :
<mud-file-item filename="raport.pdf" [size]="245760" state="uploading" />

Project an [icon] to replace the leading file glyph — a per-extension icon, or an <img ngSrc> when the preview comes from a server (previewSrc mints object URLs, which NgOptimizedImage rejects):

Example :
<mud-file-item filename="raport.pdf">
  <mud-icon icon name="file-pdf" />
</mud-file-item>

A previewSrc thumbnail still wins over the projected icon, and the error state drops the leading icon entirely so the status icon carries the row.

components.description:
Switch — an instant on/off toggle. A native <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> (the official a11y pattern) drives a styled track + thumb; the label toggles on click.

Works with BOTH forms systems:

  • Signal forms via the FormCheckboxControl contract (<mud-switch [formField]="form.notifications" /> binds checked).
  • Reactive/template-driven forms via ControlValueAccessor (boolean value).
  • Standalone via the two-way [(checked)] model.

Deliberately minimal like the official switch: one size, no invalid / readonly / supporting-text states. Associate an external message via aria-describedby when needed.

Example :
<mud-switch [formControl]="notifications">
  <mud-label>Notificări prin e-mail</mud-label>
</mud-switch>

`aria-describedby` at it instead, leaving nothing projected into the field.

functions.name: caretForDigitIndex
functions.rawdescription:
Offset immediately after the nth digit, so a re-mask restores the caret to
the digit the user was working on instead of flinging it to the end.

Task 14 needed an extra clause here — when the nth digit was the LAST one
typed and a just-auto-inserted separator followed it, the caret had to land
after that separator, or it would visibly stall one position short of where
forward typing continues. `formatMasked`'s separator is now lazy, so a
masked string always ENDS on a digit: for the last digit, `i + 1` is already
the end of the string and there is no separator left to step over. The
clause was removed with the bug that made it necessary.

functions.name: formatMasked
functions.rawdescription:
Strips everything that isn't a digit, then walks the segment spec inserting
the separator between segments. Typing `1504` yields `15/04`, so the
separator is never something the user has to press.

The separator is LAZY — emitted only when a following digit exists — exactly
as `phone-input`'s `phone-mask` does it. Appending it the instant a segment
filled (`15` → `15/`) made the field un-deletable: Backspace removes the
`/`, the re-mask puts it straight back, and the user can never delete the
month, never the day, and never clear the field with Backspace at all.

functions.name: provideMudDateLabels
functions.description:
Overrides only the keys you pass; the rest keep their English defaults.

Three shapes:

  • a plain partial — static labels;
  • a Signal<Partial<MudDateLabels>> - the calendars re-render when it changes;
  • a factory returning either - runs in an injection context, so it can inject() your i18n service:
Example :
provideMudDateLabels(() => {
  const i18n = inject(I18nService);
  return computed(() => (i18n.lang() === 'ro' ? RO_DATE_LABELS : {}));
})

functions.name: provideMudPhoneCountries
functions.description:
Sets the country list for mud-phone-input

Example :
bootstrapApplication(App, {
  providers: [
    provideMudPhoneCountries([
      'MD',
      'RO',
      { iso: 'PL', dialCode: '+48', name: 'Poland',
        mask: 'XXX XXX XXX', minDigits: 9, maxDigits: 9 },
    ]),
  ],
});

A single field can still opt out by setting its own countries.

projects/ngx-mud-ui/src/stories/componen.rawdescription:
Two ways to attach a message to a real `mud-text-input`.

**Projected** is the usual one: project a `mud-inline-message` into the
field and it wires `aria-describedby` itself, announcing it through its own
`role="alert"` wrapper.

**External** is for a message rendered outside the field, such as a summary
shared by several controls: give it an `id` and point the field's
`aria-describedby` at it instead, leaving nothing projected into the field.

Projected is the usual one: project a mud-inline-message into the field and it wires aria-describedby itself, announcing it through its own role="alert" wrapper.

External is for a message rendered outside the field, such as a summary shared by several controls: give it an id and point the field's aria-describedby at it instead, leaving nothing projected into the field.

projects/ngx-mud-ui/.storybook/compodoc-.name: isPublicApi
projects/ngx-mud-ui/.storybook/compodoc-.rawdescription:
The template API is inputs and outputs. Compodoc also reports public methods
and properties, which for these components means the `ControlValueAccessor`
plumbing every field must expose (`writeValue`, `registerOnChange`,
`setDisabledState`, ...) and underscore-prefixed internals that are public
only because a template binds them. Neither is something a consumer calls,
and both crowd out the real API — `mud-numeric-input` listed 44 rows.

projects/ngx-mud-ui/src/stories/componen.rawdescription:
`MudSegmentedControl` implements the signal-forms `FormValueControl` contract,
so `[formField]` binds the value and the disabled state. It has no error
region or `errors` input of its own — a segmented control is a view
switcher, not a field — so the message reads the field's own `errors()`
and is rendered beside it.

Pick **Hartă** to see the validator fail.

projects/ngx-mud-ui/src/stories/componen.rawdescription:
The library deliberately does NOT auto-add tooltips to truncated labels:
truncation is visual-only (screen readers get the full text), and
detecting it would couple this entry point to the CDK overlay. When a
long label is unavoidable, compose `mudTooltip` from
`ngx-mud-ui/tooltip` on the same button — the segment IS the button, so
directives stack directly. Apply it unconditionally or gate it on your
own truncation check.

@Component({
  imports: [MudProgressTracker, MudStep, ReactiveFormsModule],
  template: \`
    <mud-progress-tracker #tracker [linear]="true">
      <mud-step
        label="Identity"
        supportingText="Who you are"
        errorMessage="Complete your identity"
        [stepControl]="identity"
      >
        <form [formGroup]="identity">
          <input formControlName="name" />
        </form>
      </mud-step>
      <mud-step label="Address" supportingText="Where you live" [stepControl]="address">
        <form [formGroup]="address">
          <input formControlName="street" />
        </form>
      </mud-step>
      <mud-step label="Review">All done — review your data.</mud-step>
    </mud-progress-tracker>

    <button type="button" (click)="tracker.previous()">Back</button>
    <button type="button" (click)="tracker.next()">Next</button>
  \`,
})
export class ApplicationWizard {

projects/ngx-mud-ui/date-picker/src/lib/.name: caretForDigitIndex
projects/ngx-mud-ui/date-picker/src/lib/.rawdescription:
Offset immediately after the nth digit, so a re-mask restores the caret to
the digit the user was working on instead of flinging it to the end.

Task 14 needed an extra clause here — when the nth digit was the LAST one
typed and a just-auto-inserted separator followed it, the caret had to land
after that separator, or it would visibly stall one position short of where
forward typing continues. `formatMasked`'s separator is now lazy, so a
masked string always ENDS on a digit: for the last digit, `i + 1` is already
the end of the string and there is no separator left to step over. The
clause was removed with the bug that made it necessary.

projects/ngx-mud-ui/date-picker/src/lib/.name: formatMasked
projects/ngx-mud-ui/date-picker/src/lib/.rawdescription:
Strips everything that isn't a digit, then walks the segment spec inserting
the separator between segments. Typing `1504` yields `15/04`, so the
separator is never something the user has to press.

The separator is LAZY — emitted only when a following digit exists — exactly
as `phone-input`'s `phone-mask` does it. Appending it the instant a segment
filled (`15` → `15/`) made the field un-deletable: Backspace removes the
`/`, the re-mask puts it straight back, and the user can never delete the
month, never the day, and never clear the field with Backspace at all.

projects/ngx-mud-ui/date-picker/src/lib/.name: provideMudDateLabels
projects/ngx-mud-ui/date-picker/src/lib/.description:
Overrides only the keys you pass; the rest keep their English defaults.

Three shapes:

  • a plain partial — static labels;
  • a Signal<Partial<MudDateLabels>> - the calendars re-render when it changes;
  • a factory returning either - runs in an injection context, so it can inject() your i18n service:
Example :
provideMudDateLabels(() => {
  const i18n = inject(I18nService);
  return computed(() => (i18n.lang() === 'ro' ? RO_DATE_LABELS : {}));
})

projects/ngx-mud-ui/phone-input/src/lib/.name: provideMudPhoneCountries
projects/ngx-mud-ui/phone-input/src/lib/.description:
Sets the country list for mud-phone-input

Example :
bootstrapApplication(App, {
  providers: [
    provideMudPhoneCountries([
      'MD',
      'RO',
      { iso: 'PL', dialCode: '+48', name: 'Poland',
        mask: 'XXX XXX XXX', minDigits: 9, maxDigits: 9 },
    ]),
  ],
});

A single field can still opt out by setting its own countries.
